title: The freedom that names free choice is not freedom from servitude
source_text: XIII. Porro Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae notant libertatem de qua hic agitur, & a qua denominatur liberum arbitrium, non esse libertatem illam quae opponitur servituti, seu propriae seu Metaphoricae. Idque quoniam homines conditione servi non propterea carent libero Arbitrio; Neque etiam per peccatum eo spoliati sunt illi quos scriptura sacra vocat peccati servos.
pass_a_gloss: Further, the Doctors of the Roman Church note that the liberty of which there is question here, and from which free choice is named, is not that liberty which is opposed to servitude, whether proper or Metaphorical. And that because men who are slaves by condition do not on that account lack free Choice; Nor yet are those whom sacred scripture calls servants of sin despoiled of it through sin.
pass_b_english: The teachers of the Roman Church point out that the freedom under discussion, from which free choice takes its name, is not the freedom opposed to servitude, either literal or figurative.
Someone who is a slave by condition is not for that reason without free choice. Neither have those whom Scripture calls slaves of sin been robbed of it by sin.

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
